methods.name: Hurdle count part: zero-truncated Poisson and negative binomial maximum likelihood (pscl::hurdle)
methods.reference: pscl::hurdle(y ~ x1 + x2, dist = 'poisson' | 'negbin', zero.dist = 'binomial', reltol = 1e-15), count part polished by Newton steps on the analytic truncated score; SEs from numDeriv::hessian of the truncated log-likelihood; zero part glm(binomial) at epsilon 1e-14
quantities: theta, log theta and their SEs
count and zero log-likelihoods, total log-likelihood, AIC, BIC
methods.tolerance: MLE (validation/README.md, iterative): count coefficients 1e-8 (1e-6 on the flat theta profile), SEs and z 1e-6 (1e-5 flat), p 1e-4, theta and log theta 1e-7, SE(log theta) and SE(theta) 1e-5 (log theta 1e-4 and its SE 1e-3 on the flat profile); log-likelihoods, AIC, BIC Tol::stat(500); pscl's own optim 1e-5 (Poisson), 1e-4 (NB); counts exact

methods.name: Negative binomial null model and McFadden pseudo-R2 (pscl::pR2 on MASS::glm.nb)
methods.reference: MASS::glm.nb(y ~ 1) on the model frame, with its own theta, polished as disc_negbin; pscl::pR2 McFadden
methods.tolerance: log-likelihoods Tol::stat(n) (n = 400, 395); pseudo-R2 1e-8 relative; rows exact

methods.name: Conditional logit on unbalanced choice sets and its null log-likelihood (mlogit)
methods.reference: mlogit::mlogit(chosen ~ price + catch[ | 0]) on Fishing and on Fishing with charter removed from 300 situations, Newton-polished; null log-likelihoods: equal shares -sum ln J_i, mlogit's logLik 'null' attribute (market shares) and the constants-only MLE
quantities: coefficients and SEs on unbalanced choice sets
methods.tolerance: coefficients 1e-9, SEs 1e-8 relative; log-likelihoods Tol::stat(1182); pseudo-R2 1e-9 (constants) and 1e-10 (equal shares) relative

deviations.quantity: null log-likelihood and pseudo-R2 of a model with constants on unbalanced choice sets
deviations.note: the constants-only conditional logit fit (-1322.50 on the reference; McFadden 0.2037), the likelihood of the nested model; mlogit's market-share formula (-1497.72; 0.2969) gives probability to alternatives a situation did not offer. On balanced choice sets the two are equal and pinned against mlogit

deviations.quantity: null log-likelihood of models without constants
deviations.note: equal shares per situation, -sum ln J_i; mlogit's logLik 'null' attribute is the market-share value for every model, but summary.mlogit prints no McFadden R2 without an intercept, so no printed R number differs
